sections.heading: Syllabus Details
rows: Software development project_Dự án phát triển phần mềm
Lecture, Lab, Group Discussion, Presentation, Peer Review.AI-integrated tasks across all Software Development Life Cycle phases
Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h Project Presentation + 104h self-study
PRJ301, SWE201c or SWE202c, pass LAB211

This course guides students through the full Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) by working on a real-world team project, with an emphasis on applying AI responsibly in requirement analysis, design, implementation, and testing. Students will practice user story writing, system design, coding using MVC and OOP, workflow development, testing, and reporting. AI tools are integrated into each phase to enhance productivity and quality.

- Join the team as arranged by the teacher - Select the project topic & technology stack and get approval from teacher before implementing - Attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final presentation. - Analyze requirements, write user requirements, and create system diagrams with AI-assisted tools. - Design system architecture, database schema, and UI/UX wireframes using MVC, OOP, and AI suggestions. - Implement core features with AI-supported coding, apply coding standards, and manage source code in Git. - Develop and run unit/integration tests, using AI to suggest and refine test cases. - Deploy the application to staging, verify functionality, and prepare for final delivery. - Manage project progress, present milestones, and prepare high-quality reports with AI support.

- Requirement & Design: Miro, Lucidchart, Figma, Draw.io, ChatGPT, Gemini - Coding & Debugging: IntelliJ IDEA / VS Code / Visual Studio, GitHub Copilot, Tabnine - Database: MySQL Workbench, SQL Server Management Studio, pgAdmin -Testing: JUnit, NUnit, Postman, Selenium, AI-powered test case generators - Project Management: Jira, Trello, Notion, Git/GitHub - Deployment: Docker, Heroku, AWS / Azure / GCP, Vercel

sections.heading: 4 assessment(s)
rows: The student presents slides, gives a demonstration, and answers questions from the lecturer.
Requirement analysing, AI-assisted documentation, system architecture, initial UI, ERD

Evaluation Items: - SRS Document (30%): ≥15 pages, ≥12 user stories, complete and validated with AI + expert. - Design Artifacts (50%): ERD with ≥8 entities, valid state diagram, clear architecture, consistent UI. - Process (20%): ≥6 AI logs and 4 weekly reports with evidence.
View Rubrics Document for more details
The student presents slides, gives a demonstration, and answers questions from the lecturer.
Coding modules, database integration, AI-assisted debugging, functional testing

Evaluation Items: - Workflow Implementation (50%): Workflow 0 + Workflow 1 + Workflow 2 (main flow + ≥2 exception paths) fully functional. - Codebase & Database (30%) : Multi-layer design (e.g., MVC), complete CRUD classes, DB ≥10 tables, normalized with full PK/FK. - Process (20%) : ≥8 commits/member + ≥6 AI debugging logs.
View Rubrics Document for more details
The student presents slides, gives a demonstration, and answers questions from the lecturer.
End-to-end workflow completion, AI-assisted test case generation, UI/UX finalization

Evaluation Items: - Product (50%): Excellent if all 3 workflows (data setup, main with ≥2 exceptions, dashboard) are integrated and demo runs smoothly; fewer workflows or weak integration lowers the score. - Testing & QA (30%): Excellent with ≥25 test cases (AI + manual), ≥80% passed, full coverage; fewer cases, lower pass rates, or no AI evidence reduce the grade. - Process (20%): Excellent if 3 milestone reports, slides, full10 AI logs, and all members present; missing reports, fewer logs, or weak presentation lead to lower marks. AI Integration: Strong AI usage is required for higher levels across all criteria.
View Rubrics Document for more details
The student presents slides, gives a demonstration, and answers questions from the lecturer.
Requirement analysing, designing, coding, testing, integrating, AI usage

Final Evaluation The final exam is organized by the Exam Board, with at least two lecturers grading independently. Each team has 60 minutes for presentation and Q&A. Scores from both lecturers will be averaged. Evaluation focuses on: - Requirement Analysis (20%) – Quality of SRS, with AI-assisted requirement elicitation and validation. - System Design (20%) – ERD, state diagrams, architecture, and UI workflows, supported by AI in modeling and refinement. - Software Implementation (40%) – Completeness of workflows, structured codebase, and database design, with AI support in coding and debugging. - AI Usage and Professionalism (20%) – Transparency and responsibility in AI usage (logs, reports, validation of AI outputs), teamwork, and presentation quality.

1. Average on-going ≥ 5/10 to qualify for final 2. Finish 2 main workflows: Data Initiation and core functions 3. Fail if cheating detected (no resit) 4. Responsible use of AI tools 5. Member with active contribution score ≥ 80% — based on peer review, task tracking, and code contribution records.
